items.title: Legal AI Startup Crosby Bids for Weil Gotshal's Assets
points: 95-year-old law firm Weil, Gotshal & Manges filed Chapter 11 after partner exodus and a failed merger, not due to AI disruption.
Crosby, a startup valued at $400M, sees strategic value in acquiring the firm's brand, trademark, and internal data.

Law firms usually have zero value once top revenue-generating partners ('rainmakers') leave, but a century of legal templates and workflows could be worth tens of millions as training data for agentic AI (AI systems that can autonomously pursue goals).
The deal tests whether institutional knowledge from bankrupt firms can be systematically converted into AI training value, signaling a bet on AI-native law firms.

items.title: AWS Growth Can't Offset Amazon's Cash Burn Despite Strong Momentum
points: AWS grew 39%—its fastest pace in nearly five years—but Amazon missed overall revenue and net income targets, sending its stock down 6% after-hours and erasing over $50B in market cap.
Amazon is now $42.4B cash-flow negative over the past 12 months as AI infrastructure buildout costs exceed revenue gains.
CEO Andy Jassy projects AWS could grow over 40% annually through 2028 and reach $1T in revenue, but the near-term financial math doesn't yet work.

Intel's data center business grew 78% year-over-year, yet its stock fell 23% after-hours on weak consumer demand guidance—showing the same pattern of AI gains not yet offsetting legacy declines and capex needs.

items.title: Chinese Intelligence Reportedly Targeted Nvidia CEO Through Singapore Data Center Firm
points: The New York Times reports Trump was briefed about a year ago that Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive and suspected Chinese intelligence asset, cultivated a close relationship with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.
Trump reportedly took no action, and Jensen Huang received no defensive briefing, even though active surveillance of Alice Huang was ongoing when the story broke.
Nvidia says chip diversion allegations were 'thoroughly investigated and debunked'; Megaspeed declined to comment.

The story has united unusual political allies—Laura Loomer and Elizabeth Warren—around concerns that Chinese intelligence could influence Nvidia's chip export policies or access sensitive AI technology.

items.title: Spawn's Agentic Architecture Shows How to Abandon Traditional Org Structure
points: 10-person game studio Spawn ships 77,000 code changes monthly using persistent fleets of AI agents with ownership, memory, and real system access.
The studio spends $3.1M monthly on tokens (AI model inference costs)—30x its payroll—made feasible only after a breakthrough with the Claude Fable model.
Agents work directly in the codebase with no human pull-request reviews, running tests every 15 minutes and alignment checks hourly; of 123,000 annual changes, only about 1,000 were reverted.

Infrastructure includes 5,000 CPUs, 17TB RAM, and 150 GPUs; 'judge' models trained on two years of decision precedent let agents autonomously handle 11,000+ decisions in 8 days versus only 27 human calls.
Key insight: 'closing the loop' by making bug detection, diagnosis, and fixing fully agentic with fast feedback.

items.title: Five Principles for Agentic Teams
points: Give agents ongoing responsibility for functions (e.g., engine, bug-hunting, finance) rather than spinning them up per task, letting context carry across interactions.
Turn recurring decisions into precedent rules and train models on past patterns so agents can autonomously resolve over 99% of questions without human escalation.
Keep human attention on direction and ambition: models handle incremental improvements well but won't request transformative resources on their own.
Humans supply 'taste'—saying no even when something technically works—and manage entropy by deleting redundant work, such as scrapping 70% of the game engine in June.
